items.readable_text:
Content:
Let's remind ourselves of the names of the sides of a right triangle relative to an angle [MATH: \theta.]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/5ebbd9b8279f773a192f3830f15a4032]

Content:
The three fundamental trigonometric ratios, sine, cosine, and tangent, represent the ratios of the sides of a right triangle. The ratios are often shortened to [MATH: \sin], [MATH: \cos,] and [MATH: \tan,] and they are defined as

Content:
[MATH: \eqalign{
\sin(\theta) &= \dfrac {\text{opposite}} {\text{hypotenuse}}, \[5pt]
\cos(\theta) &= \dfrac {\text{adjacent}} {\text{hypotenuse}}, \[5pt]
\tan(\theta) &= \dfrac {\text{opposite}} {\text{adjacent}}. \
}]

Content:
For a given angle [MATH: \theta], these ratios remain the same no matter what the size of the triangle is. For example, if we were to double the length of each side of a given triangle, the values of these ratios would remain unchanged.

Content:
An easy way of remembering how to compute the different trigonometric ratios is by using the three-syllable acronym SOH-CAH-TOA. It stands for:

Content:
- SOH [MATH: \rightarrow] Sine = Opposite / Hypotenuse,
- CAH [MATH: \rightarrow] Cosine = Adjacent / Hypotenuse,
- TOA [MATH: \rightarrow] Tangent = Opposite / Adjacent.

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Remember the acronym "SOH-CAH-TOA."

  • The sine of an angle is equal to the opposite divided by the hypotenuse (S-O-H). Relative to the angle [MATH: \theta,] the opposite side is [MATH: \overline{AC},] and the hypotenuse is [MATH: \overline{BC}.] Therefore, [MATH: \sin{\theta} = \dfrac{AC}{BC} = \dfrac{3}{5}.]

  • The cosine of an angle is equal to the adjacent divided by the hypotenuse (C-A-H). Relative to the angle [MATH: \theta,] the adjacent side is [MATH: \overline{AB},] and the hypotenuse is [MATH: \overline{BC}.] Therefore, [MATH: \cos{\theta} = \dfrac{AB}{BC} = \dfrac{4}{5}.]

  • The tangent of an angle is equal to the opposite divided by the adjacent (T-O-A). Relative to the angle [MATH: \theta,] the opposite side is [MATH: \overline{AC},] and the adjacent side is [MATH: \overline{AB}.] Therefore, [MATH: \tan{\theta} = \dfrac{AC}{AB} = \dfrac{3}{4}.]

Item 10 — Example: Solving for a Variable Given a Trigonometric Ratio

Example Prompt:
Given that [MATH: \tan\theta = \dfrac{1}{4},] find the value of [MATH: x.]

[IMG: /graphics/4b342362945800bf639ee7c06cac560c]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The tangent of an angle is equal to the opposite divided by the adjacent (T-O-A).

Relative to the angle [MATH: \theta,] the length of the opposite side is [MATH: x-1,] and the length of the adjacent side is [MATH: 2x.] Therefore,

[MATH: \tan θ|= (opposite)/(adjacent); (1)/(4)|= (x − 1)/(2x); 2x|= 4(x − 1); 2x|= 4x − 4; 2x|= 4; x|= 2.]
